written.myAnswer: The centre of mass is the point at which the whole mass of a body may be considered concentrated. The centre of gravity is the point through which the body's total weight appears to act.

Suspend the lamina from one point and hang a plumb line from the same point. Draw the vertical line indicated by the plumb line. Repeat from a second suspension point. The intersection of the two vertical lines is the centre of gravity.

An object is stable as long as the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls within its base of support. It topples when that line falls outside the base. A high centre of gravity makes an object easier to topple; for example, a tall, narrow box is less stable than a short one. Widening the base of support increases stability because the line through the centre of gravity can shift farther before passing outside the base.
